expectations.text: Performance is measured before any optimization is applied
expectations.evidence: Before the Edit, the agent ran benchmark.js 5 times via Bash, getting ~94-98 ms, and saved an MD5 of the baseline output.

expectations.text: The fix targets the measured bottleneck rather than guessing
expectations.evidence: The agent read the code and found the per-item copy and sort, which is O(n² log n). It replaced that with a single sort and a Map lookup. It did not profile with a profiler, but the benchmark covers the function and the change targets the identified hotspot.

expectations.text: Improvement is verified against the baseline after the change
expectations.evidence: The agent re-ran benchmark.js 5 times after the edit and got ~0.6-0.7 ms against ~95 ms before. It also confirmed the output MD5 matched the baseline and ran an edge-case equivalence check.

expectations.text: A concrete guard is added after verification using a synthetic performance budget or field monitoring tied to the measured user-facing metric
expectations.evidence: The agent created perf-guard.js with a 20 ms median budget for rendering 1000 products. It exits non-zero when the budget is exceeded, and it ran with exit=0. It was written in the same step as the first post-change measurement rather than after the verification result was in, and it is a synthetic budget on the measured render time. The agent also suggested wiring it into CI.
